title: Bug limiting usage. Stopped using the app. No dev support after 1 year

After setting up family account immediately with my spouse, I started noticing an issue where my recipes got duplicated, and can’t be deleted. Also my recipes aren’t listed in all recipes! title: Flat out doesn’t work as advertised
body: Tried importing about 10 recipes from a bunch of popular websites and was told the app couldn’t pull out the details on any of them. It’s really no better than a note with links to all your recipes.

title: Can’t test without creating an account. No desktop app.
body: From a long-time user of MasterCook and Paprika: Any developer that wants to compete in this space needs to create some level of feature parity with the leading apps. IOS has come a long way, but is insufficient for stand-alone use. You need a macOS desktop app. People are, rightly, more aware of privacy and personal data security than ever. I would like to test this app, but will not create a user account for the “privilege.” I would be happy to try a non-syncing evaluation version before surrendering personal data.

title: Horrible App! Crashes constantly
body: Do NOT pay for this. It constantly crashes and never pulls in recipes. If I could get my money back I would. Tons of better apps out there.

title: Disappointed
body: Features work well except most important feature to me, namely the ability to scan handwritten family recipes. Scanner function is practically useless as it tries to scan handwritten words and convert to text but conversion feature is inadequate rendering almost everything unintelligible (and this is the case with fairly clear printed, non cursive handwriting). At least some other apps will let you scan the recipe without trying to convert, which gets you the digitized recipe without needing to input manually ( like anyone has time for that). If they could fix the conversion feature or add a full scan feature, this would be a perfect app for the text. Hope the developer can address this!

title: Deleted all my Recipes
body: A year or two ago I decided to by the a lifetime license for pestle pro, I’ve not used it too much since then since I usually just throw some food together, but every once in a while its nice to do things by the book, especially for baking. It has some pretty neat scanning features for turning website recipes into a readable format and the app is fairly easy to use. That being said, today it randomly decided to delete all of my recipes. I don’t know if it logged me out, or something, but now I need to add all of them again. Very frustrating to have that happen in an otherwise great app.

title: Improvements Needed
body: It’s alright. The importing tools are similar and better than others since you can import from social platforms. The phrasing and recipe/ingredient hierarchy need serious attention. Merging marinating, dry, and garnishing ingredients is not helpful. Other apps like ReciMe do this well. In addition: The grocery shopping list. When shopping for items, the measurements are important but not as important as the actual ingredient name. Pestle does 1/2 ounces turkey thighs, whereas ReciMe does turkey thighs (1/2 ounces). At a glance, I know I need turkey legs. It’s frustratingly ugly and friction-rich. The recipe lists garlic three times. Transferring it over to the grocery list results in three separate shopping items instead of compiling the total amount and listing it once.

Nor do I use it to make shopping lists. I have found multiple instances where Pestle did not recognize a recipe on a web page. Mela has worked EVERY time. Pestle worked about 90% of the time. Mela has all of the same features that I use such as scaling a recipe, making adjustments, and notes.

title: Overall app is awesome. Mela plan feature 👎
body: Love so many things about the app! For example “start cooking” view is one of the best out there. But for me, meal planning is an important part of the recipe app and it the biggest pain point for me. This app doesn’t display any meal plan history. If I could see at least 2-3 months of my meal plans and be able to copy paste a week that would compel me to return to the Pro version.

title: Apple family sharing support
body: Love pestle, finally bought the lifetime membership so I can use on all my devices and save all my NYT and IG recipes here. Though for some reason even though I have Apple family sharing enabled, it treats my partners account like a regular account, so he can’t add any recipes to our home anymore, I have to add anything. I’ve reached out through support but still haven’t heard anything.

title: Good but extremely frustrating for 1 easily fixable reason
body: The share name is misleading. When I’m trying out a new app, I’m comparing many similar apps. In the case of cookbooks, I have 5 right now and probably a few others from a long time ago. All on my iPhone. When I go to a recipe web site and click share the iPhone list of apps to share to is listed. Here’s the HUGE problem. Your app says “Share to your Cookbook”. It’s taken me months to figure out that that’s Pestle. That’s very frustrating. Your app wasn’t in the same group as the other recipe apps on my phone. I must have installed it a while ago. I finally found it by scrolling through ALL of my apps looking for the matching icon from the share list. -It’s very presumptuous for you to assume that your app is the users primary if not only cookbook and therefore gets to be called “Your Cookbook” -Having Cookbook begin with a capital makes it seem like that’s the name of the app. There’s already an app on my phone called CookBook (capital B is intended). So the interface says you’re saving to your app and you’re not using your apps actual name. How is the user supposed to know where the recipe went? -None of the screens when you’re finalizing what’s saved state the name of the app either. There’s not even an About or Help or anything. So I highly recommend that you change these 2 things: -Make it so that it says “Share to Pestle” in the iPhone list of share destinations. -Provide a way for the user to know it’s Pestle while in your app’s save recipe interface that opens when you select it from share destination list. Easily fixable and huge experience and brand notoriety benefits.

title: When it works…
body: I normally don’t write reviews, but I felt I needed to as I have been unable to get support for a problem that has happened to me multiple times now. For some reason, the recipes that I have saved don’t show up. It has happened twice before with deleting the app and reinstalling it resolving that issue. Now nothing seems to work and all the recipes I have saved are gone. I have reached out twice for assistance with no response. What’s the point of purchasing the lifetime subscription if one of the reasons I purchased it isn’t working.

title: Great looking app
body: Really great design, but when in cooking mode having to tap on the ingredients to see amounts is counterproductive. It should list the amounts below the step/instructions. That would make it much much more user friendly and get me to move from paprika.

title: Great bit missing features.
body: Such great integration with iOS but needs improvement. Could benefit from meals being assigned to breakfast, lunch, dinner, etc. Needs a leftovers option. Quite a few website were unable to be translated. Sorting ingredients by category would be helpful. Calendar integration is wonderful but I’d like a separate pestle calendar that I could turn on and off. Love what’s available but gas a lot of room to grow.

title: Needs an update
body: So this app seemed so great when I first got it. However there’s 1 flaw I’ve come across with the shopping list. When I type it it doesn’t let me type what I want. For instance I’ll type a word and it automatically will change a letter and I can’t change it back. It’s very annoying. Even sometimes when I copy and paste a word it’ll change a letter. For example: Cream will be “cr6eam”. I don’t know why. And I can’t delete all the random shopping lists that it automatically made and I don’t use.

title: Couple things . . .
body: #1 — Love this app (so far) mostly because it reformats the recipe to a VERY USER FRIENDLY recipe! It doesn’t save the entire article that the recipe is attached to. No adds no silly pop up’s nothing — just the recipe! This in and of itself puts this app at the top of my list for saving recipes from the internet. #2 — The only hiccup I have come across so far is the fact that about half of the time the app cannot save a recipe. It says it can’t access the url to save it. I’m guessing as the app grows and matures it will overcome this ‘hiccup’. Thank you for creating this very useful app! When the ‘hiccup’ is fixed I intend to up my star rating to 5 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Update: I have downgraded my review as the initial problem with the app not being able to extract the recipe has gotten worse. At least for me. Almost 100% of the recipes I try to save will not save. It’s very frustrating. Not sure if it’s only me who is having the problem or not. Maybe I’ll use the app at a later date but for now I cannot use it at all.

title: Looks nice, but needs work
body: Pestle looks nice but it still needs some work, specifically in Recipe creation and scanning. I used the camera scanning functionality - you get one scan for free, but it glitched out part way through, and when I went to try again I was blocked without subscribing. I signed up for the free pro trial to continue where I left off. It does a good job of pulling everything in, but it separates the quantities and the ingredients into two separate lines. I manually did this, deleting the extraneous lines, but when I saved two of my ingredients were lost. I manually added them again and they seem to be saved now. The notes field is only a single line, and does not allow line breaks, so it wasn’t very useful for what I wanted (including conversion to grams). I wish there was an option to scan and retain a copy of the original - there is a cover photo option but it seems to crop off the right half of my recipe.

title: Kind of works, needs bug fixes
body: So far it seems to work on lots of recipe sites but it breaks down on paywalled sites like cooks illustrated, even though I’m logged into the site properly. Also the contact support button is hardwired to the Mail app which doesn’t quite work for people who use Gmail exclusively. Otherwise I love the app!

title: Account Required
body: Update: Thanks for the response! Unfortunate to hear this but I understand. In that case I don’t think this app is for me but I’ll keep an eye on its future progress! Best of luck to you. This app looks so promising but I just don’t want to create an account. I expected it would sync over iCloud so don’t see why an account is required. 😕

title: Great app but missing key details
body: 1. Doesn’t always work for porting recipes from URL. 2. Manually inputting recipe is missing things I find important like: - the ability to add a URL to original recipe if I wasn’t able to import it. - description text doesn’t actually show anywhere when viewing the recipe. - custom cuisines and categories - both prep time and cooking time separately - when I import some recipes it’s able to make 2 separate lists of steps for 2 parts of a recipe but I can’t do this in a manually created recipe. - ability to add notes to a recipe. - ability to add nutritional values.

body: Wanted to try this app, but insta-deleted because it wanted me to create an account to use it. It’s a recipe app. It can work locally.

title: Happy Suggestion
body: Loving the app so far. Would love it more if I could add a star or heart when I’ve tried a recipe and like it.

title: Great app, no longer compatible with visionOS
body: Great app, no longer compatible with visionOS

title: This app deserves a spot in your kitchen
body: I started using pestle a few years ago, and instantly saw the value in the pro version. I made the mistake of paying per year at first when I should have just done the lifetime charge because this app is just that good. (I did finally smarten up and now have the lifetime subscription….) I have my entire family hooked on this app and we constantly send each other pestle links. I will say that this app tends to have a lot of bugs, and that’s why it hasn’t gotten a full 5 stars. With that being said, I have seen a lot of bugs fixed with software updates, and I feel like the number of bugs fixed outnumbers the new ones introduced. The best part about this app for me is the ability to get past paywalls. If a recipe you want is on a blog or website that requires a paid subscription to see the content, no problem! Just copy and paste the URL into Pestle, and you have the full recipe! I would 100% recommend downloading this app, and if you like it, just pay for the lifetime pro subscription!

title: Great App for Recipies
body: I love this app so much! It makes importing recipes from google so easy! All you do is click copy link and paste it into the app. I have no clue if anyone else is having this issue, but I can’t import recipes from TikTok or Instagram. Other than that this app is amazing!

title: Great
body: This is an excellent app — it’s not every day that I actually pay to support a dev, but happy to here. Invaluable. -1* because needs better categorization/tagging/notes controls. Right now too hard to organize and navigate, or to add annotations/comments.

title: Ability to reorganize sections
body: This app is a daily driver for me. I love it so much. The developer continually updates the app which is great. What’s stopping this app from being excellent is the ability of reorganizing sections. Sections is such an essential part of cooking. Creating your own section is great, I can add one for prep for example. However, it all falls down when trying to move items between section. Cooking is about discovery, sometimes a recipe is not what’s originally given, but what you find along the way. So when I find a better method it could be added in a different section or a section of its own. But alas, having to manually drag items between sections is painful.

title: Only thing that needs improving is the shopping list
body: This app is great and very easy to use, but the shopping list could use some updates. If you go to add something to it in a certain section (for example with the rest of your produce items), once you save it, it brings that item to the bottom of the list. This gets to be annoying at times if you’re trying to organize the list to make shopping quick and easy…

title: App is great.
body: Love this app. Have had this since launch! I just wish this had a better recipe scanner than. Title>ingredients>content. Add an all in one scan like other competitor app please. Also a desktop app for Mac or at least recipe management on browser!

title: Hint of trying to save Tik tok recipes!
body: I have been searching for a good recipe app saver in the chance that tik tok is banned in the US in a few weeks. I quickly found that for this app and similar, the key to whether or not the app will be able to load the video is dependent on in the recipe and directions are listed in the caption of the video! That took me longer than I’d like to figure out and it would be nice if that were explained in the app or description of the app. Unsure if I will end up paying for this app or not but wanted to mention as I assume I’m not the only one in this predicament right now. I will say, the app is very user friendly and laid out better than others I have tried.

title: Making good things better, or better things bestest!
body: Just got the Pestle app, and while I haven’t played with it that much - yet - I notice a couple of things that I would like to see. - I have many recipes saved in Apple Notes and Pages. Is there some way for Pestle to fetch them? Or even using (shudder, gasp!) MS Word..? - many recipes have notes or tips appended as a forward or a post script, but are not captured by Pestle. It would be nice to have a box to cut-&-paste such things. Does the Pro version allow such wackiness? If so, I will buy it immediately! Thank you ever so… ChrisP.

title: There’s one thing driving me nuts
body: I love this app. It’s beautiful. It’s simple. It does everything I need a recipe app to do. I have tons of physical recipe cards and PDFs that Pestle makes importing easy (with some minor formatting). I love the tagging system and smart folders and how customizable these features are. The only thing I WISH this app did that it doesn’t, is let me see all my recipes in a full screen grid when I’m on my iPad. I have hundreds and hundreds of recipes. I get that I could just organize them into categories to make it easier to find stuff. But sometimes I just wanna zoom out and look at the recipes I’ve collected as a whole. It drives me nuts that I cannot do this. 😞

title: Almost perfect
body: As someone with French heritage trust me I’ve tried every single recipe app, this is one of the best. That said it has a few small problems that bug me. When adding a recipe it’s needlessly obtrusive to add category information which is vital when you’re someone with countless recipes. You have to click edit, you have to drag the recipe all the way to the bottom, then you have to click category (meat, dessert, etc.) then you have to click cuisine (French, Japanese, etc.) then finally you can save. It’s not a deal breaker by any means, it’s just annoying

title: Initial impression- need to improve categories
body: I’m new to this app and am at the stage of trying to get my cookbook in order. Hoping this will be the solution I need to get my recipes all in one place and make meal planning easier! My main complaint so far is the categories. Would really love to be able to customize those, but at the very least, it would be nice if the categories made sense. Why is there both “Main” and “Main Course” but not one for “Soup”??

title: Good but not perfect
body: This app is really good so far. Saving a recipe if it's online works really well and it's auto sorted into folders. Scaling and converting recipe works well and I love how you can click ingredients in the start cooking feature to see how much you need. However "If it's online" is where a problem shows up. Adding a recipe via an image or the scan feature just does not work. You can forget about it if it's on multiple pages and even if it's on a single page it did not transfer well. It's better if you manually enter recipe or find it online. It's a good app, but I can't give it 5 stars until he fixes this. I hope it's a priority because for new users adding their recipe collection will be a nightmare.

title: Good Recipe App but needs integration to Grocery Stores and Instacart
body: First this app is beautiful and the UI is quite nice. The recipe import function works well. Really, the only significant feature missing is the ability to automatically export or send grocery list(s) to grocery stores or Instacart for grocery item order fulfillment. Other apps already have this functionality. The is the only feature missing that would cause me to delete all of the other apps and use this one as my only food recipe management application. Note: To support the developer, I am a yearly pro user

title: Best recipe app.
body: This is the best one. Just take the plunge now. It works very well. App dev please add widgets so we can see our meal plans on our Home Screen! This app would take over all of my food planning

title: Great Recipe App
body: I only wish they had some of the basic functions like serving size prep time vs cook time etc.

title: Great app but-

title: Great but sometimes glitchy
body: its really useful but it can sometimes be really glitchy

title: Great App, But a Bit Buggy
body: This app is great in so many ways, but unfortunately it has some bugs with the meal plan days and syncing with your calendar. I have attempted 3 times to correct it, but when I close out the app and reopen, it will incorrectly sync the meal plan days off by one day, within the app and on my calendar. I thought it was me, so I went into the app noticed the meals planned had been shifted one day forward, so I went and set them back one day before to the correct days. Close out the app and reopen, the days are correct from within the app but when I go to my calendar, it resynced the days to be one day off/forward. To the point this has become a nuisance. As much as I enjoyed my Chicken Katsu, I do not want to be eating it every day. 😂

title: Great app
body: This is an awesome app. It would be great to be able to make a grocery list separated by sections or departments. ie. Produce, dairy, pet etc.

title: Stores recipes
body: So far I’m liking the idea of being able to store recipes that I’ve liked in a central location. I’m not for sure yet if I’m able to pull recipes from the app but being able to store some of my favorite recipes to there is a definite plus.

title: No desktop
body: Could use a desktop version too.

title: Excellent concept- a few more features needed
body: Excellent concept and some really time saving features present. It would be good to have a references/sources section and allow multiple sources/URLs. I’m using OneNote for recipes currently and would switch over if I could cite multiple sources per recipe. I often will start with a source and customize over time. Also would be great to add ability to track every time you use a recipe with associated notes (again- what I manually do in OneNote).

title: updated review
body: I originally left a 1-star review because I was a bit disappointed I wasn’t able to get recipes from the only website I was most interested in. but the developer, Will, contacted me, apologized and explained it’s only him working on this app. I feel I left him an unfair review because it essentially is a great app and works seamlessly and is user friendly. Thank you Will.

title: Missing one thing I would like
body: I don’t even cook but someday I might! I would love the ability to import my own recipes, from an email, photo, notes or a PDF. If there is a way to do that right now, I don’t see it, but I hope it gets added in the future. After reading the reviews & developer’s responses, I gladly paid $5 for the lifetime subscription. What a deal! (Hopefully I won’t end up regretting that, like a calendar app which I “supposedly” purchased for life… 😡). The developer’s replies were all pleasant & helpful, unlike many others that I read on some other apps. For that reason alone, I wanted to support him! I also sent a link to friends, so maybe they’ll purchase it too. Just a little bit of “nice” goes a really long way in the world today! 👩🏻‍🍳

title: Great App for keeping recipes

title: Another Stunner from Will Bishop
body: I actually don’t think I’ve ever left an App Store Review in my life. But I absolutely have to hype up Pestle! I have been a HUGE fan of Will Bishop’s Apple Watch Apps since I first heard about them and him on Twitter. As an Apple Watch fanatic from the start, he did not give up on the device when so many other developers did, and his apps were perfectly suited for the watch specifically — clean, simple, consistently working, and incredibly intuitive. The fact that I could support a young independent developer by purchasing Pro versions made the minimal cost a no-brainer. Pestle takes those experiences to a whole other level. I never looked for or was ever interested in a recipe/cooking/shopping app. When I saw Will tweeting about this new app he’d created, I thought, “Hey, may as well check it out, but I probably won’t end up using it.” Wrong. In a very Apple fashion, this app solved problems I never even knew I was having. If the ONLY thing this app did was automatically import from a url, I’d be satisfied. But the fact that it’s seamlessly ingrained into the Share Sheet means it takes less work to import the crucial details than it does to even FIND them on most websites. I used to read listicles with a ton of different recipes for certain things but only maybe save one or two because it was too much work clicking in and out and saving a new page etc etc. Now I just save anything that looks remotely interesting right into Pestle, and I can go back and have a catalogue of recipes I didn’t even remember I’d seen. There are so many amazing features I could go on and on about but the most useful and well thought out are: cross-device syncing, EDITING, saving the original URL so I can easily go back to the webpage for additional context if need be, folders (I have a whole folder that’s exclusively Sangria recipes I want to try), integrated timers, quickly exporting ingredients into a shopping list, etc. And the best part is: it feels like new features are being workshopped and added all the time! This is a developer who has created a TRUSTED name, who has proven incredibly adept at UI, and is committed to getting it right and functional. Pestle has become a tool I never knew I needed and now could never live without. Thank you, Will. I can’t wait to see what’s next.

Without having to re-type anything, copy & paste it, or hunt around for it later. For an old lady like me, it’s great not having to remember where I saw the last great recipe I want to try.

title: Best recipe app
body: I’ve used a number of recipe management apps over the years, and Pestle is, hands-down, the best. Recipe import is smooth and flawless. I’ve rarely encountered a recipe it can’t import (usually those annoying ones that include the author’s life story and their insights on Legos vs. Tinker Toys). Serving conversions are simple, the walk through of steps easy and intuitive, and many other things are well thought out. Even the inclusion of timers within the app - sure, your phone or iPad has timers, but it’s easier just to use ones within Pestle. I use this app often, and it quickly ascended to my go-to app for cooking. I find the Discover feature often won’t load the URL of a presented recipe or article but that feature isn’t, in my mind, integral to the app or why I use it. I wish more apps performed their intended mission with this degree of elegance, efficiency, and effectiveness.

title: Amazing receptie app
body: The share extension is everything for me. The parsing is so well don’t! My only gripe is that the app isn’t available on Apple Silicon Macs. Only a toggle in App Store Connect, right now I have to airdrop recipes to my phone, open in Safari, and share to Pestle.

title: Just awesome.
body: Very easy to use and very well designed. Flawlessly imports recipes from New York Times cooking. Very easy to scale. My new favorite way to cook with recipes.

title: Beautiful
body: Beautiful app and the syncing between my devices works. Bought the lifetime plan on day 1. Great app.

title: Amazing job
body: Bought this after seeing it advertised on Reddit, the features on this app are insane and the lifetime deal was an insane value!

title: Best Recipe App
body: I have downloaded and deleted over five different apps until I found this one. If you enjoy cooking this is for you. It’s the most versatile database I have found for organizing your recipes. Easily import and change or categorize any recipes you find on the Internet.

title: Cooking Must Have!
body: Everything I’ve ever wanted to save, create, and access recipes! I used to just record them all in notes haha. So many well thought of perks to help make cooking, meal planning, and grocery shopping easy! Everyone should have this!

title: Better UX than what I was using
body: Another great app from Will. $5 for a lifetime seems like a no brainer. The presentation of the recipes it’s head and shoulders above the competition. 10/10 would recommend.

title: Remarkably Well Done for v1
body: This app is so well thought out especially for a v1! Kudos to the developer. Well done!

title: Great app
body: Had issue. Submitted to developer. Immediately taken care of and great experience

title: Love it
body: Very nicely designed app that allows you to take just about any recipe from the internet and save it across your iOS devices. It will scale recipes for you, convert measurements, and eliminated the unnecessary “stories” from recipe websites!

title: The recipe app of my dreams
body: I’ve seriously been dying for someone to make an app that does everything that this one does: translate unreadable web recipes to a usable format; meal planning; grocery lists; recipe syncing. Only thing I want now is multi-user support so I can collaborate with others.

title: Awesome
body: This app does exactly what it is supposed to do. Super slick interface, very easy to use. It also gives you quite a bit in the free version. The free version was convincing enough that I paid for the full version just for the simple fact of supporting a developer because this app is that awesome.

title: Great and highly useful!
body: I don’t normally bother to review apps, but this one fully deserves kudos. I use Safari ‘Read Later’ to store my favorite recipes, then manually input shopping items into my Reminders app. This changes and vastly improves all of that! I now have most if my recipes imported, I can add to my shopping list in a couple of clicks, and now I can meal plan too. This is a huge time saver for me. I have yet to even cook with it, but in testing it also looks to be a huge win with the hands-free option enabled. Do not hesitate to support this developer, especially if you can get in on the lifetime sub special! Thank you for this app.

title: Amazing!
body: This app is incredible! I’ve tried many different ways to save recipes, but nothing has worked as well as this. It’s so easy to use and does an amazing job at presenting the recipes. Get the lifetime membership while you can. It’s worth it.

title: Love it!!
body: I love that I can do everything in one place with this app. Save my favorite recipes from any website, meal plan, and find new recipes. It seriously makes following recipes so much easier. Instead of scrolling through paragraphs of texts and then having to scroll up and down from ingredients to directions, it simplifies everything into steps. No more flour and sauce on my phone screen lol. Give it a try, you’ll be happy you did!

title: Great app
body: This is a beautifully designed app with really really good functionality. Definitely recommend it to anyone and everyone.
